context: US choropleth map showing healthcare spending per capita by state, with a 5-step sequential blue quantize scale, keyboard navigation, and an alternate sortable table view
first_impression: Clean and immediately readable — one variable, one familiar geography, restrained palette with a clear west-low to northeast-high pattern.
what_works: The 5-step sequential blue ramp is well within perceptual limits and produces distinct tonal steps without color overload; the single-variable encoding keeps cognitive load minimal with no competing visual channels.
what_doesnt: Legend threshold labels are spaced too tightly and run together visually (e.g. '$9,601$10,936') making exact breakpoints hard to read; small northeastern states (RI, CT, DE, DC) are too compact to distinguish shading at a glance without hovering.
